# DataSQRL

> DataSQRL is an open-source data engineering harness for building data engineering agents designed around human control, correctness, and safety. It extends coding agents with a SQL compiler, a validator, an event-time simulator, and skills. The compiler turns SQRL scripts into complete data pipelines that integrate Kafka, Flink, PostgreSQL, Iceberg, and GraphQL, REST, and MCP APIs.

Key facts for working with DataSQRL:

- A project is one or more `.sqrl` scripts plus `*package.json` configuration files. SQRL is Flink SQL extended with `IMPORT`/`EXPORT` statements, table functions, relationships, and hints; the SQRL Language page documents only what differs from Flink SQL.
- The DataSQRL CLI is distributed as the `datasqrl/cmd` Docker image with the `compile`, `test`, and `run` commands. `compile` validates the script and generates every deployment asset, `test` runs the pipeline and the test queries and compares their results to snapshots, and `run` compiles and runs the pipeline locally in Docker.
- Configuration files are deep-merged in the order given on the command line, on top of the default configuration.
- System functions are always available; library functions must be imported with `IMPORT stdlib.<library>.<function>;`.

When to use DataSQRL:

- Use it to build data pipelines with a coding agent when correctness and human review matter: the compiler validates the whole pipeline as a relational plan, event-time replay tests catch time-dependent bugs, and the pipeline stays one SQL file a person can review.
- Use it for streaming and batch pipelines on Apache Flink with Kafka, PostgreSQL, and Iceberg, such as CDC, temporal joins, windowed aggregations, and deduplication. The same SQL runs in streaming or batch mode.
- Use it to serve pipeline results through GraphQL, REST, and MCP APIs generated from the same SQL, with authentication and authorization.
- Use it to build data products and views in an existing data lake or lakehouse, for example batch processing into Iceberg tables queried through DuckDB or Snowflake.

What DataSQRL is not:

- It is not an orchestrator or an ingestion tool. It complements Airflow, Dagster, Fivetran, and Airbyte: it reads from the Kafka topics, databases, and Iceberg tables they write to, and its compiled jobs can be scheduled with existing tooling.
- It is not a database or a runtime. It compiles to open-source engines and generates standard deployment assets (Flink compiled plans, SQL schemas and queries, Kafka topic definitions, API definitions) with no proprietary runtime.
- It does not replace the engines it compiles to. Engine settings are tuned through configuration and hints, and SQL the engine supports but DataSQRL does not yet can be passed through.

How DataSQRL compares:

- Apache Flink and Apache Spark: DataSQRL sits on top of them. It defines the whole pipeline once in SQL and compiles it into the assets each engine runs, with Flink as the processing engine.
- dbt and SQLMesh: they manage batch SQL transformations inside a warehouse. DataSQRL also covers ingestion, streaming, storage, and API serving in one model, and adds relational validation, event-time testing, and local execution of the whole stack.
- Streaming databases (Materialize, RisingWave, ksqlDB): they run incremental SQL inside a single system. DataSQRL is a compiler that splits a pipeline across a stream processor, a log, a database or table format, and an API server.
- Coding agents on their own (Claude Code, Codex, and others): DataSQRL is a harness around the agent, not a replacement. The agent keeps doing the reasoning; DataSQRL generates the seams between systems, validates the pipeline, and tests it with event-time replay.

This is the documentation of DataSQRL v0.12, the latest release.

## Overview

- [DataSQRL Documentation](https://docs.datasqrl.com/docs/intro.md): DataSQRL is an open-source data engineering harness for building data engineering agents designed around human control, correctness, and safety.

## Getting Started

- [Getting Started with DataSQRL](https://docs.datasqrl.com/docs/intro/getting-started.md): Run the DataSQRL data engineering agent with Docker and an LLM API key, or install the DataSQRL plugin for Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, or GitHub Copilot.
- [Tutorial: DataSQRL without an API Key](https://docs.datasqrl.com/docs/intro/getting-started-no-key.md): Step-by-step tutorial to build, validate, and test a data pipeline with the DataSQRL harness and Docker, without an LLM API key.

## Core Concepts

- [SQRL Language Specification](https://docs.datasqrl.com/docs/sqrl-language.md): Specification of SQRL, the extension of Flink SQL with table functions, relationships, and API definitions that DataSQRL compiles into data pipelines.
- [Connecting External Data Sources and Sinks](https://docs.datasqrl.com/docs/connectors.md): Connect Kafka, databases, files, and other external sources and sinks to SQRL scripts with CREATE TABLE and Flink connectors, including CDC.
- [Designing the Interface](https://docs.datasqrl.com/docs/interface.md): Design the GraphQL, REST, and MCP APIs and data product views that DataSQRL generates from a SQRL script, including mutations and subscriptions.
- [DataSQRL Configuration (package.json)](https://docs.datasqrl.com/docs/configuration.md): Reference for the DataSQRL package.json configuration: engines, scripts, tests, compiler options, connectors, environment variables, and merging.
- [Flink Engine Configuration](https://docs.datasqrl.com/docs/configuration-engine/flink.md): Configure Apache Flink, the stream and batch processing engine in DataSQRL pipelines: runtime mode, Flink SQL options, and an example configuration.
- [Kafka Engine Configuration](https://docs.datasqrl.com/docs/configuration-engine/kafka.md): Configure Apache Kafka, the log engine in DataSQRL pipelines: topic retention, watermarks, transactions, and key and value formats.
- [Vert.x Engine Configuration](https://docs.datasqrl.com/docs/configuration-engine/vertx.md): Configure Eclipse Vert.x, the DataSQRL API server for GraphQL, REST, and MCP, including query logging and JWT and OAuth authentication.
- [PostgreSQL Engine Configuration](https://docs.datasqrl.com/docs/configuration-engine/postgres.md): Configure PostgreSQL, the database engine that stores DataSQRL materialized views and tables for low-latency queries, including partitioning.
- [Iceberg Engine Configuration](https://docs.datasqrl.com/docs/configuration-engine/iceberg.md): Configure Apache Iceberg as a table-format engine in DataSQRL pipelines, including the catalog and warehouse of the shared iceberg connector.
- [Iceberg Query Engine Configuration](https://docs.datasqrl.com/docs/configuration-engine/iceberg-query.md): Configure DuckDB, Snowflake, Spark SQL, Redshift, and Trino as query engines that DataSQRL pairs with Apache Iceberg to create and query Iceberg tables.
- [Default DataSQRL package.json Configuration](https://docs.datasqrl.com/docs/configuration-default.md): The default DataSQRL package.json configuration that user configuration files are merged on top of, with the default value of every option.
- [DataSQRL Cloud Deployment Configuration](https://docs.datasqrl.com/docs/configuration-engine/cloud-deployment.md): Configure instance sizes, replicas, and other cloud resources for each engine when deploying DataSQRL pipelines to DataSQRL Cloud.
- [Functions](https://docs.datasqrl.com/docs/functions.md): Use Flink and DataSQRL system functions, import library functions, and write your own user-defined functions (UDFs) in SQRL scripts.
- [System Functions](https://docs.datasqrl.com/docs/functions-system-generated.md): Reference of the built-in DataSQRL system functions for JSONB, vectors and embeddings, text processing, and full text search in SQRL scripts.
- [Library Functions](https://docs.datasqrl.com/docs/functions-library-generated.md): Reference of the DataSQRL library functions for math, data processing, AI and LLM integration, and external systems, and how to import them.
- [DataSQRL Command](https://docs.datasqrl.com/docs/compiler.md): Install and use the DataSQRL command to initialize, compile, run, and test SQRL projects with Docker, including all options.
- [Compilation Output](https://docs.datasqrl.com/docs/compilation-output.md): The files the DataSQRL compiler writes to build and build/deploy, from the data model and pipeline DAG to each engine's physical plan.
- [Deployment](https://docs.datasqrl.com/docs/deployment.md): Deploy compiled DataSQRL pipelines to production with Flink, Kafka, PostgreSQL, Iceberg, and the API server, on DataSQRL Cloud or your own infrastructure.
- [Key DataSQRL Concepts](https://docs.datasqrl.com/docs/intro/concepts.md): Key stream processing concepts in DataSQRL: event time, processing time, and watermarks, and how time determines how data streams are processed.

## Examples

- [Examples Gallery](https://docs.datasqrl.com/docs/intro/examples.md): Open-source DataSQRL examples, from data products for a retail bank to self-contained pipelines for finance, healthcare, IoT, logistics, and more.

- [Deep Dive: How DataSQRL Works](https://docs.datasqrl.com/docs/deepdive.md): How the DataSQRL compiler works step by step: packaging, parsing, logical plan analysis, DAG optimization, physical planning, and API generation.
